globalRules.primaryGenerationRule: GPT Image 2 receives one structural reference state for one object per image; operational overlays and transient reactions never create an unbounded Cartesian product.
globalRules.stateCompositionRule: Runtime presentation composes one structural reference state with at most the explicitly applicable operational, interaction and transient layers while preserving identity and gameplay anchors.
globalRules.truthRule: A visual cue may never promise passability, collision, targeting, damage, repair, persistence or adaptation unless an accepted gameplay contract binds that consequence.
globalRules.evidenceBoundary: These bindings express falsifiable design intent only; retention, readability, implementation and runtime behavior remain unproven until their named human and technical gates pass.

primaryHypothesis.designContribution: Localized structural failure should let a player identify which lane-control assumption weakened without dictating the exact repair.
primaryHypothesis.intendedPlayerBehavior: After the assault, the player points to the failed bay, changes placement or protection, and voluntarily tests the revised route hypothesis.
primaryHypothesis.recognitionTest: On the weakest supported mobile view, the player identifies intact, damaged and critical states plus the failed bay without relying on color.
primaryHypothesis.decisionMetric: A non-briefed player attributes the first breach to the correct barricade region and proposes a coherent preparation change without assistance.
primaryHypothesis.failureCondition: The state looks decorative, suggests a false traversable passage, hides the repair side, or fails to produce a coherent next preparation decision.
guardrails: No permanent visual loss may erase player ownership after the assault reset.
No warning cue may claim a collision or pathing consequence that does not exist.
Repair guidance may expose the weak region but may not prescribe one mandatory solution.
primaryHypothesis.claimBoundary: The barricade supports the current failure-learning experiment; it does not prove retention, persistent history or a living-fortress system.

secondaryHypotheses.scope: A bounded replacement panel may suggest authored maintenance as a visual motif.
secondaryHypotheses.claimBoundary: The repair motif is visual narrative only and must not imply persistent repair history before the living-fortress gate opens.
